why: Polish round 2, from three committed decision files: heading-levels-2026-10-08.csv (78), ingredient-name-case-2026-10-08.csv (112) and polish-round-2-decisions-2026-10-08.csv (the rows a rule could not decide). 189 writes over 84 recipes. Part 1: 78 lifted headings go from level 2 to level 1, every one a promotion, under Andy's corrected rule plus the new stage/duration rule (import_cleanup.names_a_stage). Part 2: 71 ingredient names take Andy's `fix:` text literally, 4 `defer: heading` rows become ingredient headings (is_heading 0 to 1 only), and the 2 `group: Optional` lines lose their prefix and gain one inserted Optional heading row. Part 3: stir-fried-green-beans-with-pork's footnote becomes a note linked to step 3650 and step 3651 is deleted. Part 4: the footnote markers come off steps 3650 and 3853. Part 5: 25 notes whose text leads with a label naming their own kind, 13 stripped and 12 lifted into recipe_notes.title, all outside the baseline. Part 6: karak-chai's a/b/c lettering comes off 3 steps and homemade-pasta-dough's step 2536 loses its number and gains its capital. Everything except part 5 is baseline content and is patched in lockstep, per recipe, in one transaction. recipe_notes_original is not touched. No schema change: migration 63 on both sides.

recipe_steps.set: heading_level 2 -> 1 on the 78 ids in heading-levels-2026-10-08.csv; text on 3650 (marker off), 3853 (marker off), 2623/2624/2625 (lettering off) and 2536 (number off, first letter capitalized); row 3651 DELETED and the positions after it closed up
recipe_steps.why: Andy's corrected heading rule, his stage/duration addition, and the four row decisions in polish-round-2-decisions-2026-10-08.csv
recipe_steps.checked_by: the gate does NOT diff this table cell by cell, because recipe_steps is in tables.except. Section 4b of the go-live file diffs every cell of it against this declaration.

recipe_ingredients.set: label on the 71 `fix:` rows and the 2 `group: Optional` rows; is_heading 0 -> 1 on 3500, 5181, 5282 and 6057; one new heading row reading "Optional" inserted above ingredient 5163, with the positions after it pushed down
recipe_ingredients.why: Andy's review of every one of the 112 names, in ingredient-name-case-2026-10-08.csv
recipe_ingredients.checked_by: the gate does NOT diff this table cell by cell. Section 4b diffs every cell of it against this declaration.

recipe_notes.set: one new row on stir-fried-green-beans-with-pork linked to step 3650; text on 13 rows (the label stripped); text and title on 12 rows (the label lifted)
recipe_notes.why: Andy's call that a label restating the kind comes off and a label saying more becomes the title
recipe_notes.changes_no_baseline: notes are outside recipe_snapshots.content by Andy's ruling, so none of these 26 writes can move a baseline or mint an annotation

recipe_snapshots.set: the reason='original' entry of each of the 84 recipes, patched surgically to match the row beside it
recipe_snapshots.why: LOCKSTEP. A machine repair makes no mark, so the baseline moves in the same transaction as the row
recipe_snapshots.checked_by: short_circuit and annotations above, both declared unchanged, which is what a failed lockstep would break

sqlite_sequence.set: the AUTOINCREMENT high-water mark for recipe_ingredients and recipe_notes, each +1
sqlite_sequence.why: This round INSERTS two rows, one ingredient heading and one note, and SQLite records the last id it handed out in this table. It is bookkeeping and not content, and it is declared rather than excluded quietly because a sequence moving when NOTHING was inserted would be worth stopping for.
sqlite_sequence.checked_by: the two counts above, ingredient_lines 3572 -> 3573 and recipe_notes 176 -> 177. A sequence that moved by more than those inserts means rows were created and deleted, which those counts would hide and this would not.
